title: From AI Boom to Economic Bust
gist: Only a teaser is available: Goldin contends AI may drag on growth by concentrating wealth and opportunity in a few cities and destroying the low-cost jobs that historically fueled development, leaving much of the world poorer and more divided.

insights.claim: AI may prove a drag on growth rather than the boost tech optimists predict.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Challenges productivity-boom assumptions embedded in AI-driven equity narratives.
insights.quote: Contrary to tech optimists' rosy predictions, AI may prove to be a drag on growth.

insights.claim: AI concentrates wealth and economic opportunity in a few cities.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Points to widening geographic inequality and political backlash risk.

insights.claim: AI destroys the low-cost jobs that have historically fueled global development, which could make much of the world poorer and more divided.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Threatens the export-led development model for emerging economies.

insights.claim: The author frames the debate as between AI fantasists expecting abundance and doomers fearing existential threat and mass unemployment, and asks whether governments can mitigate catastrophe.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Useful two-pole framing for sorting AI narratives.
